newsitem.title: SWEDEN: H&M says increases market shares.
newsitem.headline: H&M says increases market shares.

text.p: Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz has increased its market shares significantly on all markets, the company's chief executive said on Thursday.
"With the figures I have seen I can say that we are winning market share," Stefan Persson told Reuters.
He added that the company increased its market shares also in countries where market development was weaker.
The key Christmas shopping season gave a favourable start to the company's 1996/1997 financial year, Persson said.
"We are happy with the start," he said.
H&M plans to set up about 50 new stores in 1997 with a large part of investments targeting its main market, Germany.
"Of those 50, there might be 25 in Germany," Persson said.
Five of the new stores are planned to be opened in Finland. Persson said he was very optimistic about these stores considering the success of the company's mail order operations in Finland.
